title: Application, MCP and diagnostics — bounded extraction packets
status: read-only census complete; no source mutated; proposed IDs and packet boundaries are placeholders for the orchestrator to renumber into the global P-sequence and fold into engineering/inventory/remediation-scope.json
coverage_note: All 20 in-scope files (12 source + 8 integration/unit test files under nemo-mcp/tests/) are assigned to exactly one packet below; test files are not extraction targets themselves and are listed as oracle evidence for the source packets they exercise. 'Diagnostics' in the issue title names the diagnostics.trace/diagnostics.replay OPERATIONS inside this same request/response contract, not a separate directory — confirmed no other diagnostics-named path exists anywhere in the bounded source ownership. engineering/application/{OPACITY_SLICE.md, MCP_INSTALL.md, transport-v1.schema.json} are pre-existing design/reference docs for this exact slice, read for context only; they are not in C07's bounded source ownership and are not claimed or modified by this census. This slice is NOT legacy debt being reverse-engineered: per OPACITY_SLICE.md it is a fresh, already-modular R08 pilot (base 582f51e, issues #905/#907-910) built by Ilya's team (owners Codexitron/Codeximator, reviewer Codexalog) as the first concrete instance of the Application/domain/adapter pattern the whole remediation program targets, deliberately scoped to one property (Motion layer opacity) before extending further.

packets.title: Transport-agnostic opacity command/query authority
packets.responsibility: DOM/transport-agnostic command+query authority for the single 'opacity' capability: request shape validation, per-write idempotency via a capped (256-entry) retained-result cache, monotonic revision counter, capped (32-entry) diagnostics trace, reentrant diagnostics.replay, and a single in-flight 'editing' mutex. Owns none of document/history/render state directly — all supplied via the ports argument passed to create().
packets.writer: sole owner of identity/retained/trace/editing (closed over per create() call; non-persisted; one instance per document lifetime, reset wholesale by documentChanged())
packets.public_api: NemoOpacityApplicationCore.create(ports) -> {handle, setInstanceId, documentChanged, historyChanged, changed, meta}; CommonJS export for Node in addition to the browser global
consumers: src/js/bootstrap/opacity-application.js (sole caller of .create(), binds the real ports)
nemo-mcp/tests/stdio_application.rs (Node harness requiring this exact production file with fake ports)
packets.oracle: nemo-mcp/tests/stdio_application.rs loads this exact file via Node require(), drives it through the compiled nemo-mcp binary over a real TCP wire round trip with deterministic fixture ports, and asserts revision/retry/history/mutation counts. Best-covered packet in this census.
packets.notes: Reentrant by design: perform()'s diagnostics.replay branch calls handle() a second time with the recorded command; the outer call deliberately leaves editing=false (`editing = request.operation !== 'diagnostics.replay'`) so the inner recursive call's own editing-guard can run — removing that special case would make every replay reject itself as 'a document edit is already in progress'. Revision bumps have two independent paths that must not double-count: the write path's `if (identity.revision === before) touch()` fallback is a deliberate no-op whenever a caller-supplied port (e.g. bootstrap's monkey-patched undo/redo) has already called touch() first during ports.history.checkpoint()/undo()/redo() — verified by tracing the call graph, not documented in a comment at either end.

packets.title: Document/history/render port bindings and legacy UI bridge
packets.responsibility: Binds NemoOpacityApplicationCore to the real running document: reads/writes go through NemoOpacityDomain (out-of-scope animation-domain module) and SMMotion; history checkpoint/undo/redo go through the app's real undo/redo stacks; repaint goes through renderLayerList/renderTimeline/updateUI/SMEngineBridge.renderNow. Also monkey-patches the four global undo-stack-mutating functions (pushUndoLayers, pushUndoActiveFrame, undo, redo) so any caller of those trips historyChanged(), and exposes legacy() so existing Motion property-editing call sites can route through the application service without themselves handling requestId/revision/instanceId.
packets.writer: sole owner of the four monkey-patched globals' wrapper closures, installed once at script-load time for the page lifetime
packets.public_api: window.NemoApplication.{handle,setInstanceId} (native transport's only entry point); window.NemoOpacityApplication.{meta,historyChanged,documentChanged,legacy} (UI's entry point)
consumers: src/js/motion.js (opacityLegacy() -> window.NemoOpacityApplication.legacy, all 5 write kinds: set/key-current/key-frame/remove/animated, lines 2706-2823)
packets.oracle: Corrected 2026-09-09 (peer review, Pollen — the original 'None' claim came from an oracle enumeration that only grepped nemo-mcp/tests/ and never this repo's own tests/). tests/application-opacity-bootstrap.test.cjs (9 test cases) loads this exact file via Node vm alongside tweens.js and application/opacity-application.js, against a hand-built fake document/state/SM (no real Paper.js document, no real Tauri), and asserts the production history stack, the cross-context guard, document replacement/stable-id assignment, and live-gesture rejection of API writes through window.NemoApplication.handle/window.NemoOpacityApplication. tests/browser/opacity-consumers.spec.cjs (Playwright) loads it for real in a browser and drives window.NemoApplication.handle against the real running app (real SM/exportJSON, real DOM) over the plain browser/no-Tauri path only — no window.__TAURI__ is present in that spec. tests/nemo-mcp-boundaries.test.cjs additionally asserts this file's module/size/layer declaration, but that is boundary/size enforcement, not behavior coverage. See known defect DEF-3 for the gap that remains real.
depends_on: src/js/domain/animation/opacity.js (NemoOpacityDomain — out of C07 scope, owned by the C02 animation/time census)
packets.notes: Script-load order (src/index.html:2360-2460) is domain/animation/opacity.js -> application/opacity-application.js -> ... -> project.js -> bootstrap/opacity-application.js (last) -> adapters/application-mcp.js. Safe today only because every consumer (motion.js/timeline.js/project.js) reads window.NemoOpacityApplication lazily inside an event handler, never at top-level script-execution time; a future top-level read introduced between line 2362 and 2459 would see undefined.

packets.title: Webview-side Tauri event adapter
packets.responsibility: Browser/webview half of the native wire. No-ops outside Tauri; otherwise fetches the real instance id from Rust (nemo_mcp_identity), binds it to the application core (setInstanceId), listens for nemo-application-request/nemo-application-cancel Tauri events, defers each request one tick (setTimeout 0) so a same-tick cancellation wins first, calls NemoApplication.handle, and posts the result back via nemo_mcp_reply. Cleans up listeners/pending timers on beforeunload.
packets.writer: sole owner of the module-private pending Map and unlisten array
consumers: src-tauri/src/application_mcp.rs (the Tauri event source on the other end of nemo-application-request/-cancel, and the command target of nemo_mcp_identity/nemo_mcp_reply)
packets.oracle: Corrected 2026-09-09 (peer review, Pollen — same root cause as the bootstrap-bindings oracle: the original enumeration only grepped nemo-mcp/tests/ and never this repo's own tests/). tests/nemo-mcp-adapter.test.cjs loads this exact file via vm.runInNewContext against a fully faked window.__TAURI__.core.invoke/event.listen (no real Tauri runtime, no real Rust process on the other end): 'browser transport does not initialize or mutate application state' (the no-Tauri no-op path) and 'native transport establishes identity before ready and cancels queued writes' (the one-tick-defer cancellation this packet's own notes describe). tests/nemo-mcp-boundaries.test.cjs additionally asserts this file's module/size/layer declaration, but that is boundary/size enforcement, not behavior coverage. See known defect DEF-3 for the gap that remains real.
depends_on: window.NemoApplication (defined by bootstrap/opacity-application.js, must load first — src/index.html:2459 before :2460, confirmed)
packets.notes: The one-tick defer (setTimeout(...,0)) is what lets a nemo-application-cancel event delivered in the same JS turn preempt a request that has not started running yet; once the deferred callback begins, a cancellation can no longer roll back an already-committed document mutation — matches OPACITY_SLICE.md's documented acceptance note ('Disconnect/cancellation does not prove that an already committed command rolled back').

packets.title: Loopback TCP listener and Tauri command surface
packets.responsibility: Owns the loopback TCP listener (OS-assigned port), per-instance registration via nemo_mcp::registry, the 3 Tauri commands the webview calls, and per-connection request/response lifecycle: read+validate a WireRequest, forward it to the webview as a nemo-application-request event, race the webview's reply against a 30s timeout and the peer disconnecting, then reply on the wire or emit nemo-application-cancel.
packets.writer: sole owner of the `pending: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String,oneshot::Sender<..>>>>` connection table and the spawned accept-loop task (capped at 32 concurrent connections via a Semaphore)
packets.public_api: 3 #[tauri::command]s registered in src-tauri/src/lib.rs:217-219 (nemo_mcp_identity, nemo_mcp_ready, nemo_mcp_reply), plus the ApplicationMcp managed state (lib.rs:215)
consumers: src/js/adapters/application-mcp.js (invokes all 3 commands, listens for the 2 events this file emits)
nemo-mcp/src/wire.rs::call (the TCP client on the other end of the socket this file listens on)
packets.oracle: None. See known defect DEF-1 — this file has no #[cfg(test)] module, is not referenced by any file under nemo-mcp/tests/, and is not exercised from any other src-tauri source file besides its own registration in lib.rs.
packets.notes: require_main() gates all 3 commands to window.label()=='main' — a second window, if one is ever added, cannot drive or observe the application service. serve_connection's tokio::select! races the webview's oneshot reply against a 30s server-side timeout AND the peer socket closing; see known defect DEF-2 for the untested silent-drop race this creates.

packets.title: Versioned wire contract (types, validation, schema generation)
packets.responsibility: The one versioned wire contract every other packet in this census imports: request/response shape, the 11-operation enum, structural (not semantic) payload admission, human-readable payload templates reused both in tool descriptions and in rejection messages, and the JSON-schema generation hooks schemars calls through #[schemars(schema_with=...)].
packets.writer: sole owner; every other Rust file in scope only calls its public fns/reads its public types, never redefines payload rules
packets.public_api: the full pub surface above, re-exported at crate root via nemo_mcp::contract::*
consumers: src/js/application/opacity-application.js (hand-mirrors this contract's request/response JSON shape and operation labels in JS — not code-shared, see entangled_with)
packets.oracle: nemo-mcp/tests/stdio_contract.rs (advertised_payload_schema_names_every_key_and_operation_template, rejected_payloads_name_the_shape_the_operation_expects, replay_payload_validates_the_nested_recorded_command, reads_keep_their_own_templates_and_identity_spelling), nemo-mcp/tests/transport.rs (mutation_needs_identity_before_transport), and stdio_roundtrip.rs (compiled_stdio_roundtrip_preserves_identity_and_errors asserts ApplicationResponse's apiVersion/requestId/instanceId echo end-to-end) exercise validate()/check_payload() through the compiled binary. engineering/application/transport-v1.schema.json is a committed snapshot of this file's generated schema; regenerated for this census via `cargo run --manifest-path nemo-mcp/Cargo.toml --bin nemo-mcp-schema` at this census's source_sha and diffed byte-identical against the committed file — confirmed not stale.
entangled_with: src/js/application/opacity-application.js (its READS/WRITES arrays are a hand-maintained JS mirror of READ_OPERATIONS/WRITE_OPERATIONS here; nothing but the shared integration test enforces the two stay in sync)
packets.notes: check_payload's recursion into a diagnostics.replay's nested `request` (lines 244-251) is the fix landed 2026-09-09 (f1fefdc) — it is the only place a payload's own sub-operation gets re-validated against its own required keys, because CommandPayload's fields are all Option so the outer deserialize alone cannot catch an incomplete nested command.

packets.title: Standalone schema-export dev binary
packets.responsibility: Standalone dev binary (nemo-mcp-schema, declared via Cargo.toml [[bin]]) that pretty-prints {apiVersion, request: schema_for!(ApplicationRequest), response: schema_for!(ApplicationResponse)} to stdout — the documented way to regenerate engineering/application/transport-v1.schema.json (OPACITY_SLICE.md:12-13).
packets.oracle: None automated. Verified for this census by actually running the binary at this census's source_sha and diffing against the committed snapshot: byte-identical.
packets.notes: Only dumps ApplicationRequest/ApplicationResponse — nemo_query's separate Query struct (server.rs) has its own distinct schema (different required fields, instance_id alias) that is live-advertised through the MCP tool listing but never appears in this binary's output or in the committed snapshot. See known defect DEF-4 (informational).

packets.title: The 3 MCP tools an external client calls
packets.responsibility: nemo_discover (fan out to every registered endpoint's capabilities, 2s timeout each, silently drop non-responders), nemo_query (reads only, rejects a write operation before it reaches the wire), nemo_command (writes only, same guard in reverse), and the shared call() that resolves an instanceId to a registered Endpoint and forwards over wire::call.
packets.public_api: the 3 #[tool]-annotated async methods, wired into the rmcp ServerHandler via #[tool_handler]; instantiated once in nemo-mcp/src/main.rs
consumers: any external MCP client (Claude/Codex) speaking rmcp's stdio transport
packets.oracle: nemo-mcp/tests/stdio.rs (nemo_discover with zero running apps), stdio_application.rs (nemo_query+nemo_command full round trip against the real application core), stdio_reconnect.rs (nemo_discover/nemo_query after a registration is replaced), stdio_rejection.rs (nemo_command rejecting an invalid write before it reaches the transport), stdio_cancellation.rs (a tool call's CancellationToken crossing the compiled MCP protocol into NemoServer::call), stdio_roundtrip.rs (identity/error preservation across discovery + a full command round trip through the compiled binary).
packets.notes: nemo_query re-validates the assembled request (request.validate()) itself before calling through, specifically so a malformed read fails as invalid_request rather than reaching wire::call and being misreported as 'instance unavailable' (comment at server.rs:150-152) — a deliberate duplicate of the check nemo_command gets for free from the same call() path, not an oversight.

packets.title: Per-user endpoint discovery directory
packets.responsibility: Per-user discovery directory resolution (NEMO_MCP_REGISTRY / NEMO_TAURI_DATA_DIR env override, else OS local-data-dir/com.strokemotion.app/mcp), reading+validating every *.json endpoint record in it (size-capped at 4096 bytes, UUID + 36-char-secret sanity check), and an RAII Registration that atomically creates its own record (create_new(true), mode 0600, parent dir 0700 on unix) and deletes it on Drop.
packets.writer: sole owner of the registry directory's file lifecycle
consumers: src-tauri/src/application_mcp.rs::start (creates one Registration per app launch)
packets.oracle: nemo-mcp/tests/transport.rs::registrations_are_private_and_removed_when_released; stdio_reconnect.rs exercises read_endpoints indirectly through nemo_discover after a registration file is replaced.
packets.notes: Drop-based cleanup is best-effort: a hard kill (SIGKILL, power loss) leaves a stale record behind. read_endpoints tolerates this without special-casing it — a stale endpoint just times out (server.rs's 2s nemo_discover timeout) and is silently excluded, never surfaced as an error. No reaper proactively deletes a long-stale record; the directory only shrinks when a live app's own Registration drops.

packets.title: Newline-delimited JSON framing and client call()
packets.responsibility: The newline-delimited JSON framing shared by both ends of the TCP connection (size-bounded via MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES on both read and write), and the client-side call() that connects, sends a WireRequest{secret, request}, reads back an ApplicationResponse, checks its apiVersion/requestId/instanceId echo the request, and races the whole round trip against both a CancellationToken and a 30s timeout (tokio::select! biased, cancellation checked first).
consumers: src-tauri/src/application_mcp.rs::serve_connection (the only caller of wire::read_json, and implicitly the peer of a client using wire::write_json/call)
packets.notes: call() validates the request BEFORE connecting (line 50) — a malformed request never opens a socket at all, which is what pre_cancelled_write_never_connects and mutation_needs_identity_before_transport actually assert. Easy to mistake for dead code since NemoServer::call() already validates upstream for nemo_command, but nemo_discover's synthesized Capabilities request reaches wire::call directly without going through that upstream check, so this inner validate() is load-bearing for that caller too.

packets.title: Process entrypoint, module root, and build-time source stamping
packets.responsibility: Process entrypoint (constructs one NemoServer over rmcp's stdio transport and waits), the crate's module root plus one public const (BUILD_SOURCE_ID, the git SHA the binary was built from, -dirty suffixed if the tree had uncommitted changes at build time), and the build script that stamps that env var and declares cargo's rerun-if-changed set (src, Cargo.toml/lock, sibling ../src and ../src-tauri/src, plus git HEAD and the current branch ref).
packets.writer: sole owner (3 tiny files bundled as one packet — none has independent responsibility large enough to extract alone)
consumers: src-tauri/src/application_mcp.rs::start (reads nemo_mcp::BUILD_SOURCE_ID into the registered Endpoint's build_id, alongside the Tauri app's own package version)
packets.oracle: None directly for main.rs/lib.rs (every nemo-mcp/tests/*.rs test spawns the compiled binary as a child process, so they exercise main.rs's wiring only incidentally, never asserting on it specifically). build.rs has no test; its output is only observable indirectly via BUILD_SOURCE_ID appearing in a discovered endpoint's buildId.
packets.notes: build.rs shells out to git at compile time and silently falls back to the literal string 'source-unknown' if git is absent or the command fails (e.g. building from a source tarball with no .git) — BUILD_SOURCE_ID is diagnostic-only (surfaced in nemo_discover's buildId), never validated or parsed by any consumer, so this fallback is safe by construction.

cross_cutting_notes: This slice is not legacy debt being reverse-engineered: per engineering/application/OPACITY_SLICE.md it is a fresh, already-modular R08 pilot (base 582f51e, issues #905/#907-910) built by Ilya's team (owners Codexitron/Codeximator, reviewer Codexalog) as the first concrete instance of the Application/domain/adapter pattern the whole remediation program targets, deliberately scoped to one property (Motion layer opacity) before extending further. Treat this census as confirming/documenting an already-clean boundary, not carving up a tangle.

Single-property coverage gap: src/js/motion.js only special-cases prop === 'opacity' in its 5 generic property-writer functions (lines 2706-2823) to route through window.NemoOpacityApplication.legacy(). Every other Motion property (position/anchor/rotation/scale, exprControls, per-vertex path, image-mesh vertex offsets...) still writes directly to its own domain module with zero Application/MCP visibility. Extending the pattern to more properties is unbuilt, not merely untested — out of scope for this census (motion.js is owned elsewhere) but material to anyone estimating the next slice's size.

Corrected 2026-09-09 (peer review, Pollen): the original oracle enumeration for this census grepped only nemo-mcp/tests/ (8 Rust files) and missed this repo's own tests/ (6 opacity/MCP-referencing JS files at this SHA), producing two false 'no oracle' claims. Actual state: src-tauri/src/application_mcp.rs (Rust/Tauri side) is the only file in this census with genuinely zero test coverage (DEF-1 — no #[cfg(test)], not referenced by any file under nemo-mcp/tests/ or elsewhere in src-tauri). src/js/bootstrap/opacity-application.js and src/js/adapters/application-mcp.js (JS/webview side) both have real oracles (tests/application-opacity-bootstrap.test.cjs, tests/browser/opacity-consumers.spec.cjs, tests/nemo-mcp-adapter.test.cjs), but every one of those oracles either fakes window.__TAURI__ entirely or runs with no Tauri present at all — none exercises the real Tauri IPC against the real compiled src-tauri binary end-to-end (DEF-3, narrowed accordingly). OPACITY_SLICE.md and MCP_INSTALL.md both already flag 'installed executable' / 'packaged desktop' acceptance as a separate, not-yet-done gate rather than an oversight, consistent with this narrower gap.

engineering/application/{OPACITY_SLICE.md, MCP_INSTALL.md, transport-v1.schema.json} are pre-existing design/reference docs for exactly this slice — read for context in this census, not in C07's bounded source ownership, not modified or claimed here.

known_defects.summary: Zero test coverage of this file's actual compiled code: no #[cfg(test)] module inside it, no file under nemo-mcp/tests/ references it (they all fake the endpoint instead, via a Node harness or Rust fixtures), and no other src-tauri source file exercises it beyond its own command registration in lib.rs:215-219.

serve_connection's tokio::select! races the webview's oneshot reply against a 30s server-side timeout. If the JS reply arrives via nemo_mcp_reply after the timeout has already fired and removed the connection_id from `pending`, nemo_mcp_reply's `pending.lock()...remove()` finds None and returns Ok(()) silently (application_mcp.rs:93-100) — the MCP client already received a cancellation, and any document write the JS side performed has no visible trace on either end. Inferred from reading both sides, not reproduced by a running test — consistent with DEF-1, no fixture exercises this file at all.
known_defects.severity: product-debt (unverified — silent-divergence risk under a slow or blocked webview)

known_defects.summary: Corrected 2026-09-09 (peer review, Pollen): the original claim of zero test coverage anywhere in the repository was false — tests/application-opacity-bootstrap.test.cjs and tests/browser/opacity-consumers.spec.cjs both exercise this file with real production logic (see corrected oracle above). The gap that is actually real and still uncovered: no oracle anywhere runs this file's document/history/render port bindings AND src/js/adapters/application-mcp.js's webview transport together against a real window.__TAURI__ and a real compiled src-tauri/src/application_mcp.rs backend. Every existing oracle takes one of three shortcuts instead — a hand-built fake document/state with no Tauri at all (application-opacity-bootstrap.test.cjs), a real browser with no window.__TAURI__ present (opacity-consumers.spec.cjs), or a fully faked window.__TAURI__.core.invoke/event.listen with no real Rust process on the other end (nemo-mcp-adapter.test.cjs, covering adapters/application-mcp.js). The packaged-desktop, real-IPC path is therefore still unverified end-to-end — consistent with OPACITY_SLICE.md/MCP_INSTALL.md's own 'installed executable' acceptance-gate note (see cross_cutting_notes).
known_defects.severity: test-coverage gap (narrowed from repo-wide to the real-Tauri-IPC path only)
